judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (same canonical coordinate, rank 0) in Strand 1 NUMBER, Sub-Strand 3 Fractions, so any developmental direction would require substantive same-rank evidence. B4.1.3.1.1 concerns generating unit fractions and locating them on a number line by partitioning the 0-1 interval (LC tags: unit fractions, number line, partition), while B4.1.3.1.3 concerns reducing given fractions to simplest form by dividing through by the HCF (LC tags: HCF, cancelling, simplest form). These are complementary fraction skills — one a part-whole/representation meaning of fractions, the other a multiplicative equivalence/factor procedure — with meaningful conceptual coherence but no evidenced dependency: HCF cancelling draws on equivalence and factors rather than on number-line placement of unit fractions, and the two sit under different Content Standards (B4.1.3.1 equivalent/improper fractions vs. the merged B4.1.3.2 comparing/adding/subtracting parent). Shared parents, weak code-prefix overlap and the single shared token 'fractions' are nomination signals only, so symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), limiting further exemplar detail.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same grain, rank 1) under Content Standard B5.1.1.3 on factors and multiples of numbers 1 to 100. The second SFI (B5.1.1.3.1, 'Identify the factors of whole numbers 1 - 100', LC tags: factors, whole numbers) is the discrete identification skill, while the first (B5.1.1.3.5, 'Recognize relationship between factors and multiples of whole numbers from 1 to 100', LC tags: factors, multiples, relationship) requires coordinating factors with multiples into a relational understanding. Fluency in locating factors of a number substantively supports success in recognizing the factor-multiple relationship, so the developmental direction runs from the second to the first endpoint; the shared parent and code prefix alone were not treated as sufficient. Same-rank direction rests on this statement-text difference in cognitive demand, not on source or code order; endpoint source evidence is truncated, which limits corroborating exemplar detail.

judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit under the same BASIC 4 Content Standard B4.1.1.1 ('quantities and place value for multi-digit whole numerals up to 100,000') in Strand 1 Number, Sub-strand Counting, Representation & Cardinality, and share the same Grade coordinate (BASIC 4, rank 0), so direction rests on statement substance rather than rank. B4.1.1.1.1 (second) has learners model number quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals with graph sheets/multi-base materials up to 100,000 (LC tags: place value, multi-digit, modelling), which establishes the positional place-value understanding of thousands, hundreds and tens. B4.1.1.1.5 (first) applies that understanding to round off/up/down whole numbers up to 10000 to the nearest thousands, hundreds and tens (LC tags: place value, rounding up/down). Proficiency in concretely modelling place value positions supports success in deciding and adjusting digits when rounding to those same positions, so the second statement builds towards the first. Evidence limitation: both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge/code context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each), so only the bounded excerpts, LCs and hierarchy were used.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (same grain, same rank 0) under Content Standard B4.1.1.3 'Demonstrate an understanding of factors, multiples and squared numbers' in Strand 1 Number. The second SFI (B4.1.1.3.1) asks learners to determine the set of factors of a given number up to 50, while the first (B4.1.1.3.6) requires representing square numbers using factors. Fluency in generating factor sets is the enabling skill for using factors to represent/identify square numbers (e.g. recognising a repeated equal factor pair), so the second substantively supports success in the first; the first extends factor work to the more complex square-number representation. LC tags corroborate the shared 'factors'/'numbers' skill core ('factors, numbers, sets' vs 'factors, representation, square numbers'). Same-rank direction rests on this substantive skill dependency, not on code order or shared parentage alone. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so exemplar detail is unavailable, but the statement texts are unambiguous.

judgment.rationale: B6.1.2.1 (Strand 1 Number / Sub-Strand 2 Number Operations, BASIC 6) requires describing and applying mental mathematics strategies and number properties for basic multiplication facts to 144 and related division facts; B6.2.3.1 (Strand 2 Algebra / Sub-Strand 3 Variables and Equations, BASIC 6) requires solving problems involving single-variable, one-step equations with whole number coefficients. Solving one-step equations with whole-number coefficients operationally depends on fluent recall of multiplication/division facts and on number properties and the inverse multiplication-division relationship named in B6.1.2.1, so proficiency in the number-operations standard supports success in the algebra standard rather than the reverse. Both are Content Standards at the same canonical BASIC 6 rank (2), so direction rests on this substantive content dependency rather than grade ordering; shared grade ancestry, weak 'b6' code prefix, and the single shared token 'number' were not treated as evidence. Endpoint source evidence is truncated (24 and 26 omitted items), which bounds but does not contradict the stated statement texts.
